content.title: Costco faces new lawsuit over membership auto-renewal notices, reports say
content.text: BEND, Ore. — After two lawsuits targeting its $4.99 rotisserie chicken and another over alleged price increases from tariffs, warehouse giant Costco is now facing a lawsuit over its annual membership. The new complaint in federal court argues that Costco violated California law regarding over its auto-renewal notices.The suit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California on behalf of plaintiff Russell George, alleges that Costco sent George a renewal notice 60 days before his membership expired, according to the website Top Class Actions.According to California’s Automatic Renewal Law, “notice shall be provided at least 15 days and not more than 45 days before the automatic renewal offer or continuous service offer renews.”The lawsuit also reportedly alleges that Costco failed to provide details such as length, price and terms of renewal and methods on how to cancel it.“Due to Costco’s untimely and deficient auto-renewal notice, the plaintiff was deprived of information he was statutorily entitled to that would have notified him of the upcoming auto-renewal and provided him with methods of cancellation,” the lawsuit reads, according to Top Class Actions.The Oregonian reports that Oregon law does not have a similar time frame standard.The lawsuit also reportedly claims George was considering considering canceling his $65 per year Gold Star membership due to lack of use.“Had the plaintiff been provided this notice in a timely manner, he would have cancelled his membership and not gone forward with the auto-renewal,” the lawsuit says, according to Top Class Actions.Central Oregon Daily News has reached out to Costco for a response. As of 4:00 p.m. Thursday, we had not heard back.This is the latest class-action lawsuit Costco is facing. The Issaquah, Wash., company was sued in January, accused of falsely advertising that its popular rotisserie chicken contains “no preservatives.” Three weeks later, a proposed class-action lawsuit was filed by an animal rights nonprofit, claiming that a Costco chicken processing plant in Nebraska suffers from salmonella contamination.Another lawsuit reportedly claims that Costco wrongfully passed the cost of President Donald Trump’s tariff duties onto customers. The lawsuit came after the U.S. Supreme Court struck down the tariffs.
